svg.text: HER POV
THE FIRST MESSAGE FORMULA
VOLUME 01 • DIGITAL EDITION
CHAPTER 03
THE C.A.R.E. FORMULA
Four principles behind a better opener
When the first draft sounds nothing like you
Daniel matches with Olivia. Her profile jokes: "My irrational fear is being
stuck in an elevator with someone who wants to make small talk." Daniel's
first idea is a generic compliment. His second is an exaggerated flirt. Neither
reflects what interested him. Finally he writes: "If we got stuck in an
elevator, would complete silence be the official rule?"
The opening is relevant and lightly playful. It isn't a guarantee of chemistry.
It simply shows a better decision: respond to the context without
performing. This fictional scenario illustrates the practical framework we call
C.A.R.E.:
Context, Authenticity, Respect, Ease.
The framework is an editorial
teaching tool, not a validated scientific method.
C — Context: Does it belong here?
Context is the connection between what you're saying and the situation. If
someone writes "I'm training for my first 10K," an opener like "How's the
training going?" belongs. A question about an unrelated subject may also be
harmless, but it ignores the strongest available invitation.
Before drafting, complete this sentence: "I'm bringing this up because ____."
If you can point to a bio, prompt, shared experience, or mutual conversation,
you probably have a starting point. If the only answer is "because I found her
attractive and searched for personal details," rethink the interaction.
Context does not make every message welcome. Platform norms and
individual boundaries matter. A friendly question inside a mutual dating-app
